name: MCP Tool Router

specs.name: call_tool
specs.description:
Run a tool from this router's catalog and return its result.

This is the only way to run the tools listed by find_tools(). It is not
the only way to reach those servers in general: if your client already
has one of them registered as its own MCP server, calling it there is
fine and cheaper — use this router for everything else.

`tool` is a STRING VALUE, not a function you can call. "owui_rag.query_knowledge"
is a handle that belongs in this parameter — calling it by that name directly
will not work, no matter what your client suggests. The real parameters of the
target tool go into `arguments` as a nested object:

    call_tool(tool="owui_rag.query_knowledge",
              arguments={"query": "Meta-Modell", "knowledge": "Psychologie & Therapie"})

If a call fails, fix the arguments and call this again — do not fall back to
raw HTTP; there is no direct access to the instances from here.

arguments.description: Object with the parameters from describe_tools(), e.g. {"law": "bgb", "paragraph": "823"}

specs.name: describe_tools
specs.description:
Full parameter schema for one or more tools from find_tools().

Pass the "instance.action" strings from the directory; several at once
are fine. Do this before call_tool() — the directory intentionally
omits schemas to keep it small.

specs.name: find_functions
specs.description:
Everything ONE instance offers — look inside a tool.

Without query_words: every function name of that instance, nothing cut
off. With query_words: only the matching functions, with what they do.
Three matches or fewer come with their parameters and an example call,
so you can call_tool() right away.

mode.description: "and" = every word must match (default), "or" = any word

specs.name: find_tools
specs.description:
Directory ACROSS all instances: which instance does what. START HERE.

Call it WITHOUT arguments to see the catalog — that is the cheap, safe
default. Pass query_words only to narrow a large catalog down; a query
that matches nothing returns everything instead of failing, so you can
never end up empty-handed.

Each line is "instance.action — what it does". Use that exact string
with describe_tools() to get the parameters, then call_tool() to run
it. To see everything ONE instance offers, use find_functions().

query_words.description: Search terms, e.g. ["law", "gesetz"]. Full handles like "gesetze_im_internet.get_paragraph" and bare instance IDs are accepted too and count as direct hits.

category.description: Restrict to one category (as shown in the listing)

mode.description: "or" = any word matches (default, recommended), "and" = every word must match

meta.description: One connection instead of many — search the tools of all running MCP instances, fetch a schema, call it. Keeps the tool list in the prompt small. Read-only.
